# Settings reference

Declared configuration for Mysti **2.0.2**, generated from the manifest and English labels. There are **199 settings**.

Use VS Code Settings and search the exact key, or edit the appropriate settings JSON. Defaults here are declarations, not your effective configuration: user/workspace overrides, provider capabilities and authority clamps still apply. An empty model override uses provider/account selection.

Descriptions mirror the manifest; [provider setup](PROVIDERS.md) and [approval contracts](NATIVE_APPROVAL.md) explain current runtime limits. For credentials and telemetry, read [privacy](PRIVACY.md) first.

[Documentation home](README.md) · [Command reference](COMMANDS.md) · [Machine-readable settings](reference/settings.json)

## general-and-providers

### `mysti.defaultProvider`

Primary AI provider for coding assistance. Switch providers anytime without losing context.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `"claude-code"` | Not declared |

Allowed values: `"claude-code"`, `"openai-codex"`, `"google-gemini"`, `"cline"`, `"github-copilot"`, `"cursor"`, `"openclaw"`, `"opencode"`, `"ollama"`, `"localai"`, `"qwen-code"`, `"hermes"`, `"continue"`, `"openrouter"`, `"kimi-code"`, `"minimax"`.

### `mysti.defaultAgent`

The agent selected when a chat panel opens. Unlike [`mysti.defaultProvider`](#mystidefaultprovider) this may be a pseudo-agent (`mysti`, `brainstorm`) that has no CLI of its own. `mysti.defaultProvider` remains the CLI backend used for delegation, brainstorm, `@agent` mentions and prompt enhancement.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `"mysti"` | Not declared |

Allowed values: `"mysti"`, `"brainstorm"`, `"claude-code"`, `"openai-codex"`, `"google-gemini"`, `"cline"`, `"github-copilot"`, `"cursor"`, `"openclaw"`, `"opencode"`, `"ollama"`, `"localai"`, `"qwen-code"`, `"hermes"`, `"continue"`, `"openrouter"`, `"kimi-code"`, `"minimax"`.

## updates

### `mysti.updates.notifyNewModels`

Show a notification when a backend publishes a model you have not seen before, with a one-click button to select it for that agent. Detection only — Mysti never switches your model on its own.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boolean` | `true` | Not declared |

### `mysti.updates.checkCliUpdates`

Check installed CLI backends against their published npm versions once a day and offer a one-click update. New models are often gated on a CLI version (GPT-6 Astra needs Codex CLI 0.153.1+). Nothing is ever installed without an explicit click.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boolean` | `true` | Not declared |

## claude

### `mysti.claude.backgroundWaitCeilingMs`

How long (ms) the headless Claude Code process waits for **background subagents/workflows** to finish before exiting, so their results are reported back through the turn (sets `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS`; requires `claude` ≥ v2.1.182). Default `600000` (10 min). `0` = wait indefinitely. Raise it if you run long background workflows. If a workflow launched via Claude Code never reports its result, first check `claude --version` is ≥ 2.1.182.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `number` | `600000` | Not declared |

Declared bounds: minimum 0; no maximum.

## checkpoints

### `mysti.checkpoints.enabled`

Snapshot the workspace before each chat turn so you can rewind code to any prior turn. Uses a private git repository stored outside your project — it never touches your own .git.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boolean` | `true` | Not declared |

### `mysti.checkpoints.maxFiles`

Skip checkpointing when the workspace has more than this many tracked/untracked files (0 = no limit). Protects very large repositories from slow snapshots.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `number` | `20000` | Not declared |

Declared bounds: minimum 0; no maximum.

### `mysti.checkpoints.maxSnapshots`

Maximum checkpoints to retain per workspace before the oldest are pruned (0 = unlimited).

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `number` | `200` | Not declared |

Declared bounds: minimum 0; no maximum.

## compaction

### `mysti.compaction.enabled`

Enable automatic context compaction when token usage exceeds the threshold

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boolean` | `true` | Not declared |

### `mysti.compaction.threshold`

Context usage percentage at which automatic compaction triggers (50-95%)

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `number` | `75` | Not declared |

Declared bounds: minimum 50; maximum 95.

### `mysti.compaction.smart.enabled`

Enable **smart compaction** (requires a connected DeepMyst account). Adds cache-aware timing, a cheap incremental compactor agent, an economic compact-vs-cache decision with a quality floor, cherry-pick retrieval over full history, and an always-on savings display. When off — or when no DeepMyst account is connected — Mysti uses the standard threshold compaction configured above.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boolean` | `false` | Not declared |

### `mysti.compaction.smart.cheapModel`

Model used by the smart compactor agent for summarization + retrieval scoring, routed through the DeepMyst gateway. A cheap, reliable model is recommended (default `claude-haiku-4-5`).

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `"claude-haiku-4-5"` | Not declared |

### `mysti.compaction.smart.minSummaryTokens`

Quality floor for smart compaction — the compacted prefix is never targeted below this size. Keeps it above the model's minimum cacheable prefix (≈4096 on Opus/Haiku) so the summary still caches, and preserves enough context for quality.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `number` | `5000` | Not declared |

Declared bounds: minimum 2048; no maximum.

### `mysti.compaction.smart.retrieval.enabled`

When smart compaction is active, allow parallel cherry-pick retrieval over the full on-disk history to pull back relevant summarized-away context. Only fires when a prompt needs buried history (gated by a free local relevance check), so it rarely adds cost.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boolean` | `true` | Not declared |

## deepmyst

### `mysti.deepmyst.gatewayUrl`

Base URL of the DeepMyst OpenAI-compatible LLM **gateway** used by smart compaction (`/v1/chat/completions`). Distinct from `mysti.deepmyst.apiUrl` (the MCP/REST host). The same `dm_` key authenticates both. Machine-scoped so a workspace can't redirect your key; the client also only ever sends it to a `*.deepmyst.com` host.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `"https://gateway.v2.deepmyst.com"` | `machine` |

### `mysti.deepmyst.apiUrl`

Base URL of the DeepMyst API used for brokered MCP connections (Plan 04). The user's `dm_` API key is sent as `Authorization: Bearer`; DeepMyst exposes MCP tools at `/api/v1/mcp/{agent}`. Machine-scoped so a workspace can't redirect your key; the client also only ever sends it to a `*.deepmyst.com` host.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `"https://api.v2.deepmyst.com"` | `machine` |

### `mysti.deepmyst.webUrl`

Base URL of the DeepMyst web app, opened in the browser for Clerk sign-in/sign-up and for managing connections.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `"https://v2.deepmyst.com"` | `machine` |

### `mysti.deepmyst.useInLocalClis`

Expose your DeepMyst MCP connections (Smithery/Composio) to your local AI CLIs (Claude Code, Gemini, Qwen, OpenCode, Codex, Cline) by writing the per-user MCP broker endpoint (`/api/v1/me/mcp`) into each CLI's MCP config, with your `dm_` key as the Bearer. **Off by default** — when on, your `dm_` key is written into those config files (including the workspace `.mcp.json`, which may be committed to git). Toggle it from the DeepMyst Connections panel.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boolean` | `false` | `machine` |

## boost

### `mysti.boost.enabled`

**Boost mode (Plan 24).** One switch that applies measured-better defaults: compaction fires earlier (profile-dependent threshold instead of 75%), smart compaction turns on (still entitlement-gated, fail-open), and un-tiered `@mysti` delegations get tier/effort routing — strong for security/review-shaped tasks, fast only for prose-shaped ones. Overlay only: values you set explicitly always win, and turning Boost off restores stock behaviour instantly. Never touches mode, access level, autonomy, or permission settings. Machine-scoped so a workspace cannot change model routing or spend behaviour.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boolean` | `false` | `machine` |

### `mysti.boost.profile`

Boost preset profile. Only applies while `mysti.boost.enabled` is on. Machine-scoped so a workspace cannot change model routing or spend behaviour.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `"balanced"` | `machine` |

Allowed values: `"economy"`, `"balanced"`, `"quality"`.

## models

### `mysti.models.autoRefresh`

Keep each agent's model list up to date automatically. A few seconds after startup — once provider discovery has settled, so it never competes with it — Mysti refreshes the model lists of every backend that supports live discovery (CLI or HTTP), staggered, and pushes the result to any open chat panel. Only lists past their cache lifetime are re-probed, so opening another window costs nothing. Disable to rely only on the bundled/curated and cached lists.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boolean` | `true` | Not declared |

## mysti

### `mysti.mysti.coordinatorModel`

**Pin** the **Mysti agent**'s coordinator to a single model, routed through the **DeepMyst gateway** using your signed-in DeepMyst account (no local key needed; a free account works). Leave **empty** (default) to rotate the curated free-model list in `mysti.mysti.freeModels` — on a rate-limit Mysti rolls over to the next free model, then to the paid `mysti.mysti.fallbackModel`. Set an id (e.g. `openrouter/openai/gpt-oss-120b:free` — the `openrouter/` prefix picks the OpenRouter provider via the gateway, or a bare gateway model like `claude-haiku-4-5`) to disable rotation. (Only used when no `mysti.openrouter.apiKey` is set — an OpenRouter key opts into OpenRouter directly instead.)

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `""` | `machine` |

### `mysti.mysti.freeModels`

Ordered list of **free** models (routed through the DeepMyst gateway) the Mysti coordinator tries when `mysti.mysti.coordinatorModel` is empty. Defaults to STRONG concrete free models (strongest first, from https://openrouter.ai/collections/free-models) rather than OpenRouter's random `openrouter/free` auto-router — the coordinator has to follow the delegation protocol reliably, and the random router can pick weak models that can't. On any transient failure — rate-limit, provider drop, 5xx, mid-stream fallback — Mysti advances to the next entry (graceful degradation), and only after all are exhausted falls back to the paid `mysti.mysti.fallbackModel`. To use the random free auto-router instead, set this to `["openrouter/openrouter/free"]` (note the doubled prefix: `openrouter/` selects the OpenRouter provider via litellm, `openrouter/free` is the router slug; a bare `openrouter/free` mis-parses to a 502). Reorder or trim to taste. Ignored when a single model is pinned in `mysti.mysti.coordinatorModel`.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `array` | `["openrouter/stealth/space-bunny-alpha","openrouter/openai/gpt-oss-120b:free","openrouter/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free","openrouter/google/gemma-4-31b-it:free"]` | `machine` |

### `mysti.mysti.subagentModel`

Model for **native Mysti subagents** (`delegate agent="mysti"`) when the coordinator names none. Empty (default) = the subagent runs on the coordinator's own model chain (whatever `mysti.mysti.coordinatorModel` / the fallback resolves to). An OpenRouter id, e.g. `stealth/space-bunny-alpha`. If the OpenRouter catalog lists it as paid, every subagent call goes through `mysti.mysti.paidBudgetPerTurnUsd` (asking when over budget) and it never runs inside a parallel batch.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `""` | `machine` |

### `mysti.mysti.advisorAgents`

Backends the Mysti coordinator asks for **advice** (`delegate agent="advisor"`), in order. The first installed one runs read-only on its strongest model, billed to the plan you already have.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `array` | `["claude-code","openai-codex"]` | `machine` |

### `mysti.mysti.advisorModel`

Paid OpenRouter model the advisor falls back to when none of `mysti.mysti.advisorAgents` is installed. One call, no tools, subject to `mysti.mysti.paidBudgetPerTurnUsd`. Empty = no paid fallback.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `"anthropic/claude-opus-5.5"` | `machine` |

### `mysti.mysti.paidBudgetPerTurnUsd`

Per-turn budget (USD) for **paid** model calls made by the Mysti coordinator's paid advisor fallback (`mysti.mysti.advisorModel`) and by native subagents whose explicit model — a `model=` the coordinator names, or `mysti.mysti.subagentModel` — the OpenRouter catalog lists as paid. Calls within it proceed; anything over it — or of unknown price — asks first. `0` (default) = every such call asks. Approval cards deny on timeout. A subagent with no explicit model runs on the coordinator's own model and is not counted here. Spend is shown in the turn footer.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `number` | `0` | `machine` |

Declared bounds: minimum 0; maximum 50.

### `mysti.mysti.maxDelegations`

Max sub-agent **delegations** per Mysti-agent run (doubled at xhigh/max effort). The coordinator's own read-only tools (read/ls/grep/diag) have a separate budget and never consume delegation slots. Machine-scoped so a workspace cannot raise your per-run spend ceiling (consistent with the coordinator-model settings).

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `number` | `6` | `machine` |

Declared bounds: minimum 1; maximum 16.

### `mysti.mysti.maxTurns`

Hard cap on coordinator **model streams** per Mysti-agent run (doubled at xhigh/max effort) — the run's spend ceiling. One stream = one turn; a delegation result, a local read-tool result, and a length-continue each start a new turn. Machine-scoped so a workspace cannot raise your per-run spend ceiling. Lower it to cap spend more tightly.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `number` | `24` | `machine` |

Declared bounds: minimum 2; maximum 64.

### `mysti.mysti.memory`

**Unified cross-backend memory** for the Mysti agent: durable project facts (learned by the coordinator via a `remember` tool) are stored per-workspace and injected into every future Mysti run — so the 14 backends behave like one agent that knows your project. Injected as untrusted, nonce-fenced data. Disable to stop persisting/injecting learnings. Review or delete individual facts with the `Mysti: View & Prune Mysti Memory` command.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boolean` | `true` | `machine` |

### `mysti.mysti.crossReview`

**Cross-vendor review** (the coordinator-only superpower): after a delegation modifies files, Mysti dispatches a *different-vendor* backend (e.g. Anthropic wrote it → OpenAI or Google reviews it) in READ-ONLY mode to catch bugs the writer's own model would miss — decorrelated blind spots no single-vendor agent gets. `advisory` runs one review per run and feeds findings back to the coordinator; `off` (default) disables it. Costs one extra read-only delegation; requires ≥2 different-vendor backends installed.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `"off"` | `machine` |

Allowed values: `"off"`, `"advisory"`.

### `mysti.mysti.verify`

Verification loop for the **Mysti agent**: after a delegation modifies files, Mysti automatically runs a read-only editor-diagnostics check and prompts its coordinator to verify the change (e.g. run the project's tests/build) before answering — the single biggest 'did it actually work' quality lever. `off` disables it.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `"suggest"` | `machine` |

Allowed values: `"off"`, `"suggest"`.

### `mysti.mysti.localExecution`

**Standalone execution for the Mysti agent (Plan 19).** When `on`, the `@mysti` coordinator gets its OWN gated `write` / `edit` tools AND a **sandboxed `bash`** tool (run tests/builds/linters) — so it works even with no CLI backend installed. Every op goes through the **same permission gate** as CLI backends (default-deny in ask modes), is **workspace-scoped** (secret files blocked), and is **checkpointed** (undoable); `bash` additionally runs in an **OS sandbox** (macOS Seatbelt / Linux bwrap — no network, writes limited to the workspace; on platforms without a sandbox only genuinely read-only commands run). Destructive commands (`rm`, `sudo`, `git push --force`, `curl|sh`, container/daemon control, …) are hard-blocked; chained/compound commands and anything not on the read-only allowlist ALWAYS require explicit approval (a command auto-runs only when it is read-only-safe, non-compound, sandboxed, and a capable coordinator model is pinned). Machine-scoped on purpose: a workspace cannot enable it. Disabled in untrusted workspaces and in plan / read-only tiers. A pinned capable coordinator model (`mysti.mysti.coordinatorModel`) is recommended.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `"off"` | `machine` |

Allowed values: `"off"`, `"on"`.

### `mysti.mysti.bashNetwork`

Whether the `@mysti` agent's sandboxed `bash` tool may access the **network**. Default `off` (the sandbox blocks all egress) — the safest posture, since the coordinator model is prompt-injectable. Turn `on` only if you need the agent to run installs/downloads itself; it widens the attack surface. Requires `mysti.mysti.localExecution` = `on`. Machine-scoped.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `"off"` | `machine` |

Allowed values: `"off"`, `"on"`.

### `mysti.mysti.skills`

**Agent catalog for the Mysti agent (Plan 20).** When set to `prose`, the `@mysti` coordinator can **search and read** the project's reusable working practices - the bundled personas/skills/roles plus any you have written in `.mysti/agents/` - instead of re-deriving the same procedures every session. Retrieval only: it reads files you already have and calls nothing, so there is no permission card. What it reads is injected as **reference material, not instructions**, and only integrity-verified bundled content is ever trusted further (workspace- and user-authored files are fenced). Costs nothing when off, and nothing when fewer than 8 artifacts exist. `full` additionally turns on the **authoring and execution** capabilities - the `publish` and `skillrun` directives (Plan 20 Phases 3-4). `full` is **necessary but not sufficient**: those tags are added to the parser only when ALL of the following also hold - `mysti.mysti.localExecution` is `on`, the turn is not in a plan mode and not `read-only` access, the workspace is **trusted**, and this machine has a working OS sandbox (macOS Seatbelt or Linux `bwrap`; Windows and Linux without `bwrap` have none, so `full` grants nothing extra there). When any one is false the tags are not recognized at all, so the capability does not exist rather than existing and erroring. `publish` additionally requires two forced confirmation cards, and `skillrun` runs a host-owned command shape with arguments passed by file. Machine-scoped so a workspace cannot enable it.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `"off"` | `machine` |

Allowed values: `"off"`, `"prose"`, `"full"`.

### `mysti.mysti.mcpTools`

**External MCP tools for the Mysti agent (Plan 19).** When `on`, the `@mysti` coordinator can call the external tools you've **connected via DeepMyst** (Gmail, Slack, Trello, Notion, databases, …), discovered live through the DeepMyst broker. Every call is an un-undoable network side effect (sending mail, creating a ticket), so it **always** requires an explicit approval card — it is never auto-approved, even in full-access or autonomous-aggressive. Only your already-connected tools are callable (a model-invented tool name is refused); results re-enter the model as untrusted, nonce-fenced data. Requires a signed-in DeepMyst account and a trusted workspace. Off by default; machine-scoped so a workspace cannot enable it. Budget: `mysti.mysti.maxMcpCalls` per run.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `"off"` | `machine` |

Allowed values: `"off"`, `"on"`.

### `mysti.mysti.maxMcpCalls`

Max **external MCP tool calls** the `@mysti` agent may make per run (each still requires explicit approval). NOT effort-scaled. Machine-scoped so a workspace cannot raise your per-run external-call ceiling. Requires `mysti.mysti.mcpTools` = `on`.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `number` | `6` | `machine` |

Declared bounds: minimum 1; maximum 32.

### `mysti.mysti.fallbackModel`

Optional **paid** gateway model the Mysti agent falls back to when **every** free model (`mysti.mysti.freeModels`, or the pinned `mysti.mysti.coordinatorModel`) is unavailable. Empty (default) = free-only: when every free model is rate-limited or offline, Mysti says so and offers **Choose model** instead of spending. Set e.g. `claude-haiku-4-5` to spend DeepMyst credits as a last resort.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `""` | `machine` |

### `mysti.mysti.visualTools`

Let the Mysti agent SEE your running app: render it in a real browser and read back console errors, failed requests, layout/contrast problems, the accessibility tree and a screenshot. Requires a trusted workspace and Playwright browsers (npx playwright install chromium). Off by default — it starts a dev server and a browser.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `"off"` | `machine` |

Allowed values: `"off"`, `"on"`.

### `mysti.mysti.maxVisualLooks`

Maximum times the Mysti agent may look at the running app in a single run (doubled on high effort).

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `number` | `6` | `machine` |

Declared bounds: minimum 1; maximum 24.

## openrouter

### `mysti.openrouter.apiKey`

**Optional power-user opt-in.** An OpenRouter API key (`sk-or-...`) to run the **Mysti agent**'s coordinator on OpenRouter **free** models INSTEAD of the DeepMyst gateway. Leave empty (default) to run through your DeepMyst account. Get one at https://openrouter.ai/keys. Machine-scoped so a workspace can't read or redirect it; only ever sent to `openrouter.ai`. The `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` environment variable is used as a fallback.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `""` | `machine` |

### `mysti.openrouter.coordinatorModel`

Model the Mysti agent uses for its own coordination (decompose/synthesize). `auto` (default) discovers a currently-available OpenRouter **free** model at runtime (the roster rotates, so ids are never hardcoded). Set an explicit id (e.g. `openai/gpt-oss-120b:free`) to pin one, or `openrouter/free` to use OpenRouter's free meta-router.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `"auto"` | `machine` |

## collab

### `mysti.collab.maxConcurrent`

Maximum collaborators (advisor/critic/reviewer/coworker) dispatched at once when using @agent:role mentions or the /consult, /review, /critique, /panel commands. Higher values run more agents in parallel but use more resources.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `number` | `3` | Not declared |

Declared bounds: minimum 1; maximum 8.

## permission

### `mysti.permission.timeout`

Seconds to wait for permission approval (0 = no timeout, requires explicit action). Machine-scoped: a workspace cannot shorten it to fast-track an auto-accept.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `number` | `30` | `machine` |

Declared bounds: minimum 0; no maximum.

### `mysti.permission.timeoutBehavior`

Behavior when a permission request times out. Machine-scoped (security): a repository's workspace settings cannot flip this to auto-accept to silently approve delegation/edit writes — the workspace-raises-authority escalation review[0] closed.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `"auto-reject"` | `machine` |

Allowed values: `"auto-accept"`, `"auto-reject"`, `"require-action"`, `"semi-autonomous"`.

Declared bounds: minimum 10; maximum 300.

## debug

### `mysti.debug.performanceLogging`

Log detailed performance instrumentation to the Debug Console with the `[Mysti][perf]` prefix: activation and provider-init timings, panel time-to-usable, time-to-first-token, per-chunk render cost percentiles, and heap samples. When off, only a few coarse timings (activation, panel ready, first token) are recorded. Only enable when diagnosing performance issues.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boolean` | `false` | Not declared |

### `mysti.visualTest.serverReadyPattern`

Regex pattern to detect when the dev server is ready (matched against stdout). Machine-scoped and length-capped so a cloned repo cannot inject a catastrophically-backtracking pattern.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `"localhost:\\d+\|ready in\|compiled successfully\|VITE\|started server on"` | `machine` |

### `mysti.visualTest.allowedOrigins`

Origins the visual-testing browser may reach. Loopback-only by default: a browser that can fetch arbitrary URLs and screenshot them back to a model is an exfiltration channel. An entry without a port allows any port on that host. Cloud metadata addresses are blocked even if listed.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `array` | `["http://localhost","http://127.0.0.1","http://[::1]"]` | `machine` |

### `mysti.visualTest.allowModelDevServerCommand`

Allow the AI to supply the dev-server shell command. Off by default — the command comes from mysti.visualTest.devServerCommand or your package.json, so a prompt-injected model has no command to name. Turning this on re-introduces a model-to-shell path, gated by a modal confirmation.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boolean` | `false` | `machine` |

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `"off"` | `machine` |

Allowed values: `"off"`, `"safe"`.

## desk

### `mysti.desk.enabled`

**Desk — cross-machine teamwork (off by default).** Lets the Mysti agent knock on a paired teammate's Desk: ask where something lives, or consult their agent about their codebase. Every call shows you exactly what will leave this machine before it goes. Machine-scoped: a cloned repository can never turn this on.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boolean` | `false` | `machine` |

### `mysti.desk.serve`

**Answer teammates' requests.** When off, Desk works one-way: you can ask paired teammates, but nothing on your machine ever answers. Turning it on binds a loopback-only listener; peers still need a pinned key and an explicit grant.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boolean` | `false` | `machine` |

### `mysti.desk.servingBudgetUsdPerDay`

Hard daily ceiling on what answering ONE teammate may cost you. Checked before a request is served and enforced mid-answer, so a runaway peer stops rather than accumulating.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `number` | `0.5` | `machine` |

Declared bounds: minimum 0; no maximum.

### `mysti.desk.minRetentionClass`

The weakest model-retention class you will let a teammate's question be processed by. If their Desk cannot meet it, your request is refused **before it leaves this machine**.

| Type | Declared default | Declared scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `"zero-retention"` | `machine` |

Allowed values: `"zero-retention"`, `"logged"`, `"training-permitted"`.
